subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Should the durable fix for this issue be owned inside the embedded runner, or should agent-core expose a generic control-flow error contract for non-terminal recovery signals?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the current candidate fix changes reusable agent-core failure semantics; that boundary choice needs maintainer intent before this issue can be considered solved.

options.title: Formalize the agent-core seam
options.body: Expose or document a generic agent-core control-flow contract and keep tests proving real errors still emit failure events.

options.title: Keep recovery runner-owned
options.body: Handle the mid-turn signal inside the embedded runner boundary so agent-core does not gain a hidden failure-suppression protocol.

options.title: Accept the current sentinel after proof
options.body: Allow the current PR shape once live proof is added, with maintainers owning the changed Agent failure-event semantics.

recommendation.title: Formalize the agent-core seam
recommendation.body: Expose or document a generic agent-core control-flow contract and keep tests proving real errors still emit failure events.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the original mid-turn precheck feature and the broader related PR, making them the clearest feature-history route for the boundary choice.
